cases.purpose: When several matching processes share one start time (a verified three-way tie plus an older and a newer process), pkill -n and -o signal the same process as procps pkill.
cases.oracle: procps-ng 4.0.4 pkill run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags) and of the shape of stderr (empty or text; diagnostic wording differs by design); fixture end states are read back with kill -0.

cases.purpose: pkill reports a delivery failure (EPERM on a process owned by another user, PID 1 of the VM) without signalling it: nothing succeeds gives status 1 with a diagnostic, signal 0 and -c behave the same way, and with an owned process also matching the pattern the owned process is signalled and the status reflects the partial success.
cases.oracle: procps-ng 4.0.4 pkill run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags) and of the shape of stderr (empty or text; diagnostic wording differs by design); fixture end states are read back with kill -0.

cases.purpose: A target that vanishes between selection and delivery (the kernel answers ESRCH for that PID, injected by a seccomp errno filter around the tool) is silent and not counted: with only that target the status is 1, with another live target the status and -c count reflect only the successful signal.
cases.oracle: procps-ng 4.0.4 pkill run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags) and of the shape of stderr (empty or text; diagnostic wording differs by design); fixture end states are read back with kill -0.

cases.purpose: killall diagnoses an EPERM delivery failure on a process owned by another user (PID 1 of the VM) with status 1 and no signal sent, still signals an owned process named in the same request with status 0 for that partial success, and treats a target that vanished between lookup and delivery (kernel ESRCH injected for that PID) silently: status 1 when it is the only target, 0 when another target is signalled.
cases.oracle: Requirement text (status 1 only when nothing succeeds; ESRCH silent); psmisc 23.7 fails a whole request on any failure and delivers with a different syscall, so it is not the oracle. Kernel facts: ownership from /proc/1/status, liveness from kill -0, ESRCH from a seccomp errno filter on kill(2) for one PID.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout derived from the requirement text and kernel facts read by the case.
cases.stdout:
pid1-foreign-owner=yes pid1-name-unique=yes
== killall -USR1 python3
rc=1 stdout=empty stderr=text
pid1-still-running=yes
== partial EPERM
rc=0 stdout=empty stderr=text
state: a=dead
== ghost-only
rc=1 stderr=empty
state: g=alive
== ghost+real
rc=0 stderr=empty
state: g=alive r=dead

cases.purpose: pkill -c counts only requests that succeeded: an ESRCH-injected target alone counts 0 with status 1, with another live target it counts 1 with status 0, and signalling PID 1 (EPERM) alone counts 0 with status 1.
cases.oracle: Requirement text (count and status reflect only successful requests); procps pkill counts matches, so it is not the oracle. ESRCH from a seccomp errno filter on kill(2) for one PID; EPERM from PID 1 being owned by another user.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout derived from the requirement text and kernel facts read by the case.
cases.stdout:
pid1-foreign-owner=yes pid1-name-unique=yes
ghost-only count=0 rc=1
state: g=alive
ghost+real count=1 rc=0
state: g=alive r=dead
eperm-only count=0 rc=1

cases.purpose: Several NAME operands and duplicate operands select the union of processes once: each selected process receives exactly one signal even when its name is given twice or three times, and a second operand naming other processes is signalled too.
cases.oracle: Requirement text; signal receipt is counted by the target itself (a SIGUSR1 handler appending one line per delivery).
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and facts read from the fixture's own /proc and files; psmisc killall has no usable counterpart for these forms, so no reference tool takes part.
cases.stdout:
triple operand rc=0
deliveries c1=1 c2=1
double operand deliveries c1=2 c2=2
two names twice rc=0
state: a=dead b=dead

cases.purpose: killall -f handles an empty argument (the joined command line ends in a space and matches only with it), a process with an empty command line (zombie) is neither matched nor fatal, and an exact command line longer than 4096 bytes matches while the same line with its last byte changed does not.
cases.oracle: Requirement text; the expected command lines are built by the case from the same argument vector it passed to the fixture.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and facts read from the fixture's own /proc and files; psmisc killall has no usable counterpart for these forms, so no reference tool takes part.
cases.stdout:
joined-line-has-empty-argument-slot=yes
empty-argument-collapsed rc=1
state: e1=alive
prefix-only rc=1
state: e1=alive
exact-with-empty-argument rc=0
state: e1=dead
zombie-present=yes zombie-cmdline-bytes=0
no-match-with-zombie rc=1
empty-line-pattern-does-not-crash rc-ok=yes
state: zp=alive
long-line-bytes>4096=yes

state: big=alive

state: big=dead

cases.purpose: killall -u NAME resolves the account name through the passwd database: inside a mapped user namespace the fixture runs as uid 0, so -u root selects it, another real account (daemon) selects nothing with status 1, and a numeric uid and an unknown name behave consistently.
cases.oracle: Requirement text plus /etc/passwd of the guest (root is uid 0, daemon is uid 1) and the fixture's own /proc/PID/status Uid.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and facts read from the fixture's own /proc and files; psmisc killall has no usable counterpart for these forms, so no reference tool takes part.
cases.stdout:
fixture-uid-in-namespace=0
passwd-root=0 passwd-daemon=1
-u daemon rc=1
state: x=alive
-u unknown rc-nonzero=yes
state: x=alive
-u 1 rc=1
state: x=alive
-u root rc=0
state: x=dead
-u 0 rc=0
state: y=dead

cases.purpose: The psmisc killall options -l, -q, -w, -I, -r, -g, -y, -o and -v are accepted or rejected exactly as psmisc 23.7 does: signal listing, quiet no-match, wait for exit, case-insensitive names, regular-expression names, process-group delivery, younger/older-than selection and verbose reporting.
cases.oracle: psmisc 23.7 killall run by the reference bash side against the same fixture processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags) and of the shape of stderr (empty or text; diagnostic wording differs by design); fixture end states are read back with kill -0.

cases.purpose: Malformed or missing process records are skipped fail-closed: with a synthetic /proc (bind-mounted over /proc in a private mount namespace) holding a non-numeric entry, a record with no comm, a record with a truncated stat, an empty directory and one valid record for a real fixture process, only the valid record's process is signalled and the status is 0.
cases.oracle: Requirement text; the synthetic tree is built by the case and the one valid record points at a real owned process whose liveness is read back.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and facts read from the fixture's own /proc and files; psmisc killall has no usable counterpart for these forms, so no reference tool takes part.

cases.purpose: When /proc cannot be opened at all (a private root without /proc) killall exits with the documented fatal status 3, distinct from 1 for no match and 2 for usage, and signals nothing.
cases.oracle: Documented exit-code contract of the tool (0 success, 1 no match, 2 usage, 3 fatal); the missing /proc is created by a private root holding only the binaries.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout against expectations derived from the requirement text and facts read from the fixture's own /proc and files; psmisc killall has no usable counterpart for these forms, so no reference tool takes part.
cases.script:
export CAND=$BASH
R=$PWD/newroot
/usr/bin/mkdir -p "$R/usr" "$R/opt/bashos-parity" "$R/work" "$R/tmp"
exec /usr/bin/unshare --user --map-root-user --mount -- /usr/bin/bash -c '
R=$1; shift
/usr/bin/mount --rbind /usr "$R/usr" && /usr/bin/mount --rbind /opt/bashos-parity "$R/opt/bashos-parity" || echo MOUNT-FAIL
for l in lib lib64 bin sbin; do [ -e /$l ] && /usr/bin/ln -s "usr/$l" "$R/$l" 2>/dev/null; done
/usr/bin/mkdir -p "$R/dev" && /usr/bin/touch "$R/dev/null" && /usr/bin/mount --bind /dev/null "$R/dev/null" || echo MOUNT-FAIL-DEVNULL
/usr/bin/cp ./body.sh "$R/work/body.sh"
exec /usr/sbin/chroot "$R" "$CAND" --noprofile --norc /work/body.sh
' _ "$R"
